cases.name: well-configured-link
cases.desc: A device that did everything SPEC.md 2 asks: link-layer payload raised to match the MTU, 2M PHY, 15 ms interval.
cases.note: conn_interval is in 1.25 ms units, so 12 is 15 ms.

cases.name: mtu-without-data-length
cases.desc: A large ATT MTU over the default 27-octet link-layer payload. Conforming, decodable, and roughly three times the radio airtime per byte.
cases.note: This is the condition SPEC.md 2.1 exists to prevent and which a client cannot observe from its own BLE stack on any platform. It is a diagnostic, not a reject: the device is not malformed, it is expensive.

cases.name: asymmetric-data-length
cases.desc: Link-layer payload negotiated asymmetrically: the device may send 251 octets but may only receive 27. Legal, and the two fields are distinct.
cases.note: The only vector where ll_max_tx_octets and ll_max_rx_octets differ. Without it, a decoder that reads both from the same offset passes the whole corpus -- the tx/rx pair is otherwise symmetric in every case, which is exactly the kind of hole mutation testing finds and review does not.

cases.name: phy-not-determinable
cases.desc: A controller that does not expose its PHY. The phy bit is clear, so phy_tx and phy_rx MUST be reported absent -- NOT decoded as LE 1M.
cases.note: LE 1M is 1 and there is no zero member, precisely so that a zeroed byte cannot pass for the most common PHY.

cases.name: stale-values-behind-cleared-bits
cases.desc: A non-conforming device that clears every validity bit but leaves the previous values in the bytes. A decoder MUST report every field absent on the strength of the mask alone, and MUST NOT read LE 2M or a 247-byte MTU out of them.
cases.note: Not byte-canonical, so the round-trip asserts that a conforming encoder NORMALISES these bytes to zero. Every validity bit is clear in one case deliberately: this is the only coverage the link_params encoder's gating rule gets, and a case that cleared just one bit would leave the other three gates untested — which is exactly how the gps_fix encoder gate went uncovered in the first corpus.

cases.name: nothing-determinable
cases.desc: A stack that exposes none of it. Every field is zero AND every validity bit is clear; a client MUST conclude 'unknown', not 'MTU 0 on no PHY'.

cases.name: unknown-phy-value
cases.desc: A PHY value from a future Bluetooth revision. A decoder MUST report it unknown and MUST NOT fall back to LE 1M.

cases.name: reserved-validity-bit-set
cases.desc: A future minor set link_validity bit 9. A decoder MUST ignore the unknown bit and decode every known field normally.

cases.name: short-payload
cases.desc: 15 bytes. A truncated control response MUST be rejected whole.

cases.name: long-payload
cases.desc: 17 bytes. link_params is a fixed-size record with no extension mechanism, so trailing bytes MUST be rejected.
